questions.question: Which procedure had the highest total over the 6-month period?

questions.passage: A hospital trust has 3,600 staff. 2,400 are female. Of the female staff, 18% work part-time. Of the male staff, 12% work part-time.
questions.question: How many staff work part-time in total?
questions.explanation: Female part-time = 2,400 × 0.18 = 432. Male staff = 3,600 - 2,400 = 1,200. Male part-time = 1,200 × 0.12 = 144. Total part-time = 432 + 144 = 576.

questions.passage: A patient requires morphine PCA at 1 mg per demand, with a lockout interval of 5 minutes. The maximum dose in 4 hours is 30 mg. The morphine solution is 1 mg/mL.
questions.question: What is the maximum number of demands a patient could make in 4 hours based on the dose limit?
questions.explanation: Maximum dose = 30 mg. Each demand = 1 mg. Maximum demands = 30 ÷ 1 = 30.

questions.passage: An MRI scanner performs scans taking 30 minutes each, with 10 minutes between scans for preparation. The scanner operates from 08:00 to 18:00.
questions.question: How many scans can be completed in one day?
questions.explanation: Total time = 10 hours = 600 minutes. Each scan cycle = 30 + 10 = 40 minutes. 600 ÷ 40 = 15 cycles. 15 × 30 + 14 × 10 = 450 + 140 = 590 minutes ≤ 600. One more scan: 590 + 30 = 620 > 600. So 15 scans.

questions.passage:
The table shows hospital-acquired pressure ulcers by ward:

| Ward | Patients | New Pressure Ulcers | Grade 3-4 Ulcers |
|------|----------|---------------------|-------------------|
| Medical | 320 | 16 | 4 |
| Surgical | 280 | 10 | 2 |
| Elderly Care | 180 | 15 | 6 |
| Neurology | 150 | 8 | 3 |
| Oncology | 200 | 6 | 1 |
questions.question: Which ward has the highest rate of new pressure ulcers per 100 patients?
questions.explanation: Medical: 16/320×100=5.0%. Surgical: 10/280×100=3.6%. Elderly Care: 15/180×100=8.3%. Neurology: 8/150×100=5.3%. Elderly Care is highest at 8.3%.

questions.passage: A hospital operates 40 theatres. Theatres are allocated to specialties in the ratio general surgery:orthopaedics:ENT:other = 3:2:1:2.
questions.question: How many theatres are allocated to orthopaedics?

questions.passage: A hospital's prescribing data shows that antibiotics account for 28% of all prescriptions. Of the antibiotics prescribed, 35% are broad-spectrum. Total prescriptions last year were 45,000.
questions.question: How many broad-spectrum antibiotic prescriptions were there?

questions.passage: A patient requires a heparin lock flush. The standard flush is 5 mL of normal saline containing 10 units/mL of heparin.
questions.question: How many units of heparin are in one 5 mL flush?
questions.explanation: Heparin concentration = 10 units/mL. Volume = 5 mL. Total heparin = 10 × 5 = 50 units.
